target_customer: Oncologists and clinics treating late-stage cancer patients, with patients paying through an affiliated clinic
problem: Doctors lack a data-driven way to pick which of more than 150 targeted cancer drugs will work for a given patient, so many get ineffective, toxic treatment. Oncobox ranks drugs from tumor DNA and RNA profiles.
business_model: Diagnostic test sold through affiliated clinics, with a lab that processes tumor samples

founders.name: Andrew Garazha
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder/CEO on the YC page; background not found in an opened source.

founders.name: Anton Buzdin
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder/CSO on the YC page; background not found in an opened source.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs omics profiling, bioinformatics algorithms and clinical validation, and the company's own site shows trials running through 2023.

defensibility.rationale: The site reports a US patent in 2023 and a gene expression reference built from healthy tissue in 2020, but diagnostic rivals were well funded.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large tumor profiling companies existed; no source I opened shows them copying or acquiring Oncobox.

market_need_then: The YC page cites a study of 900 late-stage patients in which targeted therapy effectiveness rose from 25 percent to 64 percent, a company claim not independently checked.

branding.domain_note: Uses oncobox.com per the YC page.
branding.brand_signature: Tagline: tailor the right cancer drug to each patient (per a directory listing)

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand. Several similarly named oncology companies (Oncobit, OncoDxRx) create confusion in search.

outcome_analysis: Oncobox is still active after YC S17 with a small team and its own site reports a 2018 platform launch, a 250-patient prospective trial finished in 2023 and a US patent the same year. No priced funding round or exit was found, so it looks like a slow science-driven diagnostics company with limited public traction data.
notes: PitchBook (via search snippet) lists only a $120K Y Combinator deal dated 2017-08-21; this is the standard YC deal and not recorded as a round. Competitor list left empty: the 2017 competitor search returned only undated directory pages. Do not confuse with OncoDxRx or Oncobit. Company site claims are self-reported.
